channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Red Hat Releases .NET 9.0 Update with Security Fixes
item.description: Red Hat released a .NET 9.0 update for RHEL 10 to fix multiple security issues. The update addresses several vulnerabilities with CVSS scores marked Important, though no specific CVE IDs are cited; the flaws could enable exploitation of the .NET runtime. Red Hat advises installing the package from standard RHEL repositories immediately and verifying checksums to ensure integrity.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for Red Enterprise Linux 10 to address multiple security bugs. The update fixes several kernel vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, and is rated as Important by Product Security. Administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:99133 package immediately to mitigate the identified flaws and ensure system reboot.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 10, fixing multiple security issues that could enable privilege escalation or denial of service. The advisory labels the update Important and lists CVSS scores, but omits CVE IDs. Apply the patch promptly to close the flaws, as it includes bug fixes and enhancements that address the reported weaknesses.

item.title: Red Hat Issues .NET 10.0 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a .NET 10.0 security update for RHEL 10, addressing multiple vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution via the .NET runtime. The update contains fixes for several CVEs, each with a CVSS base score, but no active exploitation reported. Red Hat recommends applying the RHSA-2026:99143 update immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: ChromeOS LTS‑150 Patches Critical Use‑After‑Free
item.description: Google released ChromeOS LTS-150, patching numerous high‑severity CVEs including a critical CVE‑2026‑126879 use‑after‑free in the layout engine. The update addresses 18 CVEs such as CVE‑2026‑126901, CVE‑2026‑126856, and CVE‑2026‑126887, all of which could lead to code execution or denial of service.

item.title: Baker Tilly Clients Informed of Third‑Party Breach
item.description: Baker Tilly Advisory Group notified clients that a provider breach exposed personal information of clients and their dependents. The incident involved unauthorized access to sensitive data, including names, addresses, and financial details, though the full scope remains under investigation. Clients should monitor accounts, change passwords, and review security practices while Baker Tilly coordinates with the provider to assess impact.

item.title: Unit 42 Reveals AI‑Powered Red Team Tool Usage
item.description: Unit 42 identified adversaries deploying AI‑powered red team tools, such as ARTEX, to automate reconnaissance, credential harvesting, and lateral movement. These tools use large language models to generate phishing content, craft credential‑dump scripts, and orchestrate multi‑stage attack chains. Defenders should enable AI‑aware detection, enforce least‑privilege access, deploy MFA, and run regular red‑team simulations to validate controls.

item.title: ScreenConnect Malware Breaches MSPs, Targets Customer Devices
item.description: ConnectWise investigated a malware campaign that leveraged compromised ScreenConnect environments to deploy rogue remote‑access clients to customer devices of managed service providers. The attacks enabled attackers to gain remote control over client systems, potentially exfiltrating data and installing additional malicious payloads. ConnectWise recommends MSPs update ScreenConnect to the latest version, enforce strict access controls, and monitor for unauthorized remote‑access activity.

item.title: Red Hat Releases c-ares Security Update for RHEL 10.2
item.description: Red Hat has released a security update for c-ares on RHEL 10.2 EUS, addressing multiple vulnerabilities with a CVSS base score available in the CVE references. The update is classified as Important by Red Hat Product Security, implying a high severity impact on DNS resolution functionality. Security teams should apply the c-ares update immediately to mitigate the identified vulnerabilities.

item.title: Red Hat Issues qt6-qtbase Update for RHEL 10.2
item.description: Red Hat has issued a security update for qt6-qtbase on RHEL 10.2 EUS, addressing multiple vulnerabilities with CVSS base scores listed in the CVE references. The update is marked as Important by Red Hat Product Security, indicating a high severity impact on Qt framework functionality. Apply the qt6-qtbase update promptly to protect against the disclosed vulnerabilities.

item.title: Arctic Wolf Highlights Agentic AI in 2026 Security Operations
item.description: Arctic Wolf’s 2026 Agentic Security Operations Report details how agentic AI collaborates with expert analysts to streamline incident response workflows. The integration reduces investigation time by up to 40 % and boosts detection accuracy, enabling quicker threat containment. Teams should evaluate agentic AI platforms, integrate them with SOAR, and train analysts to interpret AI‑generated hypotheses.

item.title: Greeter Attack Chain Leaves 'Hello' Trail in Cloud Logs
item.description: Researchers identified a new cloud attack chain named Greeter, in which adversaries embed 'hello' messages in log files to obscure their activity. The technique masks lateral movement and persistence indicators, making forensic analysis more difficult and delaying incident response. Defenders should enable log integrity monitoring, correlate anomalous 'hello' entries with known threat patterns, and apply stricter log retention policies.

item.title: eMudhra Revokes Eight CA Certificates After Key Mishap
item.description: eMudhra revoked eight intermediate CA certificates after discovering improper private key handling during certificate generation. The mishandling exposed the possibility of unauthorized certificate issuance, but no active exploitation has been reported. eMudhra has issued revocation notices, is reviewing its key management procedures, and will implement additional safeguards to prevent future incidents.

item.title: AI Enhances Cyber Resilience Competition
item.description: The article argues that AI technologies amplify both threat capabilities and defensive options, making rapid recovery a competitive advantage. It highlights how machine learning can detect anomalies faster, yet also enables adversaries to craft more sophisticated phishing and malware campaigns. Security teams should adopt AI‑driven monitoring, continuous testing, and adaptive response frameworks to mitigate evolving risks.

item.title: CVE-2026-125926 - Server-side request forgery in the server registration and update API in mcp-gateway-registry
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-180-AWS Publication Date: 11/11/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: MServer-side request forgery (SSRF) in the server registration and update API in Amazon mcp-gateway-registry before 1.35.0 might allow an authenticated remote user to send requests from the gateway to internal network services and cloud instance metadata endpoints and read the responses via a crafted request Impacted versions: >= v1.0.3 AND Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.

item.title: AWS mcp-gateway-registry Privilege Escalation via API
item.description: Amazon mcp-gateway-registry’s external management API lacks authorization, letting an authenticated user elevate to registry administrator. The flaw, present in versions 1.0.9–1.24.7, allows a crafted group import request to grant administrator scope to the attacker’s identity group, giving control over all registered gateway assets. AWS released a patch; security teams should upgrade to 1.24.8 or later and verify group import permissions.

item.title: Notion Breach Exposes AI Chat Transcripts
item.description: Notion revealed a breach at Fireworks AI that exposed AI chat transcripts from a few workspaces. Unauthorized access to Fireworks AI’s storage leaked user‑generated chat content, though no credentials were compromised. Notion advises users to review logs and reset passwords, while Fireworks AI has released a patch to secure the data.

item.title: N-able N-central Platform Offline Over 33 Flaws
item.description: N-able’s N-central RMM platform was taken offline after the discovery of 33 critical flaws that enable attacker takeover via public exploits. The vulnerabilities lack a single CVE identifier but collectively allow remote code execution and privilege escalation on affected installations. N-able released a hotfix; administrators should apply the update immediately and monitor for unauthorized access attempts.

item.title: Chrome Extended Stable Update 156.0.8078.100 Released
item.description: Google Chrome released Stable channel build 156.0.8078.100 for Windows and Mac, rolling out over the next weeks. The update includes security patches, but the full list of changes is available in the release log, and users are encouraged to review it. Users should install the update via browser settings or wait for automatic rollout to ensure protection against known vulnerabilities.

item.title: Chrome Stable Channel Updated to 157.0.8103.78
item.description: Google Chrome updated the Stable channel to build 157.0.8103.78 for Windows, Mac, and Linux, with rollout scheduled over the coming weeks. Security changes are included, and a list of modifications can be found in the release log, with users advised to review the details. Installation can be performed manually via browser settings or will occur automatically, ensuring users receive protections.

item.title: 2026 Agentic Security Operations Report Highlights AI Benefits
item.description: The 2026 Agentic Security Operations Report shows how enterprises use AI‑powered security operations to detect threats faster. The study reports a reduction in alert noise and a 35 % increase in analyst efficiency through AI‑driven prioritization. Organizations should integrate AI platforms with existing SOAR tools, train analysts on AI outputs, and monitor for false positives.

item.title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
item.description: Threat actors are deploying GSocket on compromised Linux servers to keep encrypted remote access after the original vulnerability is patched. Learn how to detect, investigate, and remediate this activity.

item.title: Apache HTTP Server Critical RCE CVE-2026-119618
item.description: Apache HTTP Server contains a critical RCE flaw identified as CVE-2026-119618. The vulnerability, affecting 64% of cloud environments, permits remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted requests, with no authentication required. Immediate patching is advised; administrators should apply the latest globally Apache HTTP Server update and verify configuration hardening.

item.title: Yodl Buffer Over-Read Causes Denial of Service
item.description: Ubuntu identified a buffer over-read in Yodl that could be triggered by malformed input. The flaw may allow an attacker to crash Yodl, leading to a denial of service, though no active exploitation has been reported. Users should update to the latest Yodl package via Ubuntu repositories; no additional workarounds are required.

item.title: SNMPTT Allows Remote Command Execution via Unsanitized Traps
item.description: Ubuntu discovered that SNMPTT fails to sanitize trap data passed to EXEC, PREEXEC, and unknown_trap_exec commands. A remote attacker could exploit this flaw to run arbitrary shell commands, potentially compromising the host system without authentication. Apply the latest SNMPTT update from Ubuntu repositories immediately, promptly; no additional mitigations are necessary.

item.title: Vanderbilt Restores Systems After Alleged Data Theft Attack
item.description: Vanderbilt University is restoring campus technology following a cyberattack that attackers claim stole student and employee data. The incident involved unauthorized access to university systems, but the university has not confirmed any data exfiltration. Security teams should review access logs, enforce multi‑factor authentication, and apply any pending vendor patches to strengthen defenses.

item.title: Red Hat Releases .NET 8.0 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for .NET 8.0 on RHEL 8, fixing vulnerabilities that could let attackers compromise application integrity. The advisory rates the update as Important, with CVSS scores linked to each CVE, indicating moderate to high risk but no confirmed exploitation. Apply the .NET 8.0 update immediately following Red Hat’s guidance to mitigate the identified flaws.

item.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
item.description: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St.

item.title: Ubuntu Updates MySQL to Patch Security Issues
item.description: Ubuntu released updates for MySQL, addressing multiple security issues discovered in the database engine across several releases. The patches upgrade MySQL to 8.4.13 on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, 9.7.4 on 26.10, and backport fixes to 22.04 and 24.04, potentially introducing incompatibilities. Administrators should apply the updated packages immediately and review release notes for any required application adjustments.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for RHEL 8
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for Red Enterprise Linux 8 addressing multiple moderate‑impact security issues. The update fixes several kernel bugs identified by CVE references, each with a CVSS base score indicating moderate severity; no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:99015 package to mitigate the vulnerabilities and review the CVE links for detailed impact.

item.title: PAN-OS Sensitive Info Disclosure CVE-2026-0331
item.description: A sensitive information disclosure flaw in Palo Alto Networks PAN‑OS lets attackers retrieve confidential configuration data via unauthenticated API calls. The vulnerability, CVE‑2026‑0331, exploits improper input validation in the management interface, yielding a medium‑severity exposure without credentials. Palo Alto released a patch in the latest PAN‑OS update; security teams should apply it or restrict API access.

item.title: Chromium Update Addresses CVE-2026-113971
item.description: Palo Alto Networks issued a Chromium update addressing a high‑severity flaw that could enable remote code execution via malicious web content. CVE‑2026‑113971 exploits a buffer overflow in the rendering engine, allowing attackers to run arbitrary code without user interaction. Apply the latest Chromium patch or disable the vulnerable feature to mitigate the risk until a vendor‑issued fix is released.

item.title: PAN‑OS GlobalProtect Authorization Bypass CVE‑2026‑0325
item.description: Palo Alto Networks disclosed CVE‑2026‑0325, an authorization bypass flaw in PAN‑OS GlobalProtect. The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to gain privileged access to the VPN portal, with a CVSS score indicating low impact; no active exploitation has been reported. Palo Alto recommends applying the latest PAN‑OS update that patches CVE‑2026‑0325 to prevent unauthorized access.

item.title: PAN‑OS GlobalProtect Privilege Escalation CVE‑2026‑0327
item.description: Palo Alto Networks identified CVE‑2026‑0327, a privilege escalation flaw in PAN‑OS GlobalProtect. The bug permits an authenticated user to elevate privileges on the VPN appliance, with a CVSS score reflecting low severity; no exploitation evidence exists. Apply the vendor’s latest PAN‑OS patch that addresses CVE‑2026‑0327 to eliminate the escalation vector.

item.title: PAN‑OS Panorama RCE CVE‑2026‑0330
item.description: Palo Alto Networks disclosed CVE‑2026‑0330, an authenticated remote code execution flaw in PAN‑OS Panorama. The vulnerability allows a logged‑in attacker to execute arbitrary code on the Panorama server, with a CVSS score indicating medium severity; no active exploitation has been reported. Install the latest PAN‑OS update that patches CVE‑2026‑0330 to prevent remote code execution.

item.title: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
item.description: Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers used codename MDASH to investigate Linux kernel vulnerabilities, resulting in 59 upstream bug reports, 33 assigned CVEs, and 38 merged fixes. The research includes eight demonstrated local root privilege-escalation exploits and examines the challenges of turning AI-generated findings into validated vulnerabilities and upstream fixes.

item.title: Maersk Breach Exposes Legacy System Data
item.description: Maersk confirmed that a threat actor accessed a legacy local system inherited from a prior acquisition and exfiltrated data. The breach coincided with a WhiteArmor ransomware campaign demanding a $5 million payment, though the ransomware did not encrypt Maersk files. Maersk has engaged incident response teams, applied security patches, and is monitoring for further compromise.

item.title: Zoom Workplace Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation CVE
item.description: Zoom Workplace for Windows is vulnerable to CVE-2026-108186, an unauthenticated remote privilege escalation flaw triggered by improper input validation. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.6, enabling attackers to elevate privileges without authentication and potentially compromise affected systems. Zoom has released software updates to address the vulnerability; security teams should apply the patch immediately to mitigate risk.

item.title: Hackers Could Exploit MCP Server Supply Chain Weaknesses to Steal API Keys and Administrator Credentials
item.description: Security teams that run AI coding assistants may be exposing their most powerful credentials without knowing it. A new study shows that Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers can quietly change their own code after they are set up.

item.title: .NET Elevation Privilege CVE-2026-105544
item.description: Microsoft announced an informational update for CVE‑2026‑105544, an elevation of privilege vulnerability affecting the .NET framework. The flaw allows local users to gain higher privileges by manipulating the runtime configuration, but no active exploitation has been reported. Microsoft has not released a patch yet; administrators should monitor for future advisories and apply any subsequent fixes when available.

item.title: .NET DoS Vulnerability CVE-2026-109475
item.description: Microsoft issued an informational notice for CVE‑2026‑109475, a denial‑of‑service flaw in the .NET framework. The vulnerability permits local users to trigger a crash by sending malformed input to the runtime, but no active exploitation has been observed. No patch has been released; administrators should watch for future updates and apply any subsequent fixes when available.

item.title: Microsoft Updates Product List for CVE-2026-114159 RCE
item.description: Microsoft updated its product list for CVE-2026-114159, a Visual Studio remote code execution vulnerability that could allow attackers to run arbitrary code. The update is purely informational, providing no new patch or exploit details, and does not indicate active exploitation. Security teams should review the updated product list, confirm affected installations, and apply any forthcoming patches when released.
